A morphism between two functors: the usual form is 'morphisme de foncteurs'. The singular may be the author's usage, since he also writes 'champ de vecteur' in the singular (pages 35, 36, 41). That form is not reported. The TeX keeps the printed reading.

The preceding sentence derives this formula from the smoothness of the fibre at the generic point of E_o and from 2.28 (moduli of smooth proper curves of genus p: dimension 3p-3). So the formula concerns E_o = p^{-1}(E) in T_o. dim(E) = m_o^E(s) is a local invariant and does not depend on p. Only dim(E_o) = 3p-3 lets (2.29.1)-(2.29.3) prove 2.27: dim E = 3p-3 - [3(p-δ(s))-3 + m_1(s)] = 3δ(s) - m_1(s). The TeX keeps the printed reading.

C~ is smooth of arithmetic genus p~ = p - δ(s). Hence χ(C~, T_{C~/k}) = (2-2p~) + 1 - p~ = 3 - 3p~, and -χ(C~, T_{C~/k}) = 3(p-δ(s)) - 3, not its negative. The equivalent form -[3-3(p-δ(s))] would also be correct. With the printed sign, dim H^1(C, T^1_{C/k}) would be negative for large p, and (2.29.1)-(2.29.2) would not give 2.27. With the corrected sign they give dim E = 3δ(s) - m_1(s). The TeX keeps the printed reading.

note: 2.32 concerns the component E, of dimension M_o^E, over whose generic point the deformation is smooth. Over E the formal moduli of (C,X) have dimension M_o^E + #X - M_1, and the analogue of 2.28 equates this with 3p-3+#X, the dimension for smooth curves of genus p with #X marked points. M_o is the dimension of the whole of T, and only M_o^E gives 2.32 (3p-3 = M_o^E - M_1). The TeX keeps the printed reading.
